 Order

The present petition filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 707/2021,
under Sections 498A/406/377/354/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Dabri, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi.
2. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 28.11.2020 as per Muslim rites and customs.
3. No child was born out of the said wedlock.
4. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties resided separately from 03.06.2021.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against the petitioner no. 1 (husband),
petitioner no. 2 (brother-in-law) and petitioner no. 3 (sister-in-law).
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in pursuance of the Settlement Agreement dated 06.07.2022, parties arrived at settlement before the Mediaiton Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi.

sentences.text: It is further stated that the parties are living together, at their matrimonial home, since 06.08.2022.

The terms and conditions of the aforesaid settlement agreement are as under:
"5.

After mutual discussions, both the parties have voluntarily, peacefully and amicably settled all their disputes without any coercion, pressure, undue influence,
force, misrepresentation or mistake, with respect to the present case as well as above connected matter on the following terms and conditions- (a) The complainant/ wife and respondent/husband shall live together at their matrimonial house at Flat No. 007, H Block. Delhi- 99 Society, near Koyal Enclave.
Loni Bhopura road, Ghaziabad District, UP. 201005.

For the said purpose, the respondent/husband will bring the complainant/ wife from her parental house at New Jankipuri to their matrimonial house on within two months from today (b) The Respondent/ husband shall bear all the house hold expenses including ration, water, LPG,
electricity bill medical expenses of complainant/ wife.

(c) The Respondent husband and/ or his family members shall not quarrel with complainant wife or cause her any physical or mental harm (d) The parents and other family members of both the parties shall not interfere in their matrimonial life.
(e) Both the parties shall live together peacefully and amicably and they will give due love and respect to each other.
(f) The complainant/ wife shall withdraw the present case after four months from today.

(g) The applicant shall move appropriate petition for quashing of FIR No. 707/2021 u/s 498A/ 406/
34 IPC, PS: Dabri.
The complainant/ wife shall cooperate in the same.
6. Both the parties shall make appropriate statements before the concerned court and shall cooperate with each other in all the proceedings so as to give effect to this settlement.
7. Both the parties undertake that they shall be bound by the terms and conditions as mentioned above.
8. In case, any of the above party does not abide by the terms and conditions of this settlement, the other party shall be at liberty to take appropriate action as per law.
9. Both the parties shall bear their respective cost of litigation."

Dabri.

7. The Complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled and she is living with petitioner no. 1 since 06.08.2022 at their matrimonial home and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed against the petitioners.
8. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

9. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303, Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceedings."
10.

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 707/2021, under Sections 498A/406/377/354/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Dabri, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi.

11. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 707/2021, under Sections 498A/406/377/354/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Dabri, New Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the Court of Ms. Divya Yadav, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dwarka Court, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
12. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
13. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
AMIT SHARMA, J MARCH 22, 2023/
